steps.message:
Before I touch it: this is a breaking change to a published contract, so I want a yes first.

`routes/users.js:6` is the only place `userId` appears — the rename itself is one word. But the README says:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

Renaming in place means every one of those three consumers reads `undefined` for `userId` the moment this deploys. The iOS app is the sharp edge — shipped builds can't be updated in lockstep, so 3.2+ clients in the field break until users upgrade. The nightly partner export is the silent one: it likely won't error, it'll just start emitting rows with a missing/blank user identifier.

There's no consumer code in this repo, so the rename here can't be coordinated with them — this change is only safe alongside a client rollout or a version bump.

How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return both userId and user_id from GET /users. Existing consumers keep working; new ones can adopt user_id. Deprecate and remove userId once the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the partner export have all migrated. Non-breaking, ships today.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: What the README prescribes: leave GET /users as-is and add a v2 route that returns user_id. Clients move over on their own schedule. Largest change — new route and wiring.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Straight rename at routes/users.js:6, exactly as asked. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS 3.2+ builds, and the nightly partner export on deploy. Pick this if the consumer rollout is already coordinated.

steps.message:
`routes/users.js:6` — `userId` → `user_id`. Field name only; `u.id` and the rest of the shape are untouched, and `GET /users` now matches `/orders`' snake_case.

No tests in the repo, so nothing was run. `userId` no longer appears anywhere in the tree — grep is clean.

Reminder of what this means on deploy, since you've taken the breaking path: the web app, shipped iOS 3.2+ builds, and the nightly partner export will all read `undefined` for the identifier until they're updated. The export will likely fail quietly rather than error. Worth making sure the client rollout lands first or same-day.
